# EnterpriseGlue v0.26.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.25.0`.

## Highlights

- **database-bootstrap:** Adds a signed, default-off PostgreSQL managed-shard bootstrap artifact that creates only the exact v0.24.2 schema predecessor and rejects ambiguous or drifted databases.
- **frontend-authentication:** Prevents anonymous signup from probing or refreshing a browser session while preserving login restoration and protected-route session recovery.

## User and administrator impact

- Anonymous signup no longer emits expected unauthorized session requests or related browser-console noise.
- Login pages still restore valid cookie sessions, and protected application routes continue to refresh expired access before redirecting to login.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Existing installations do not enable this artifact; continue to use the signed 0130-to-0131 compatibility bridge.
- A provisioning controller may run the bootstrap once only after verifying its signed release subject and immutable contract, then proceed through the normal owner migration and verify-only runtime gates.

## Configuration

- Managed-shard bootstrap is disabled unless EG_MANAGED_SHARD_BOOTSTRAP_ENABLED is exactly true and the target is pooled PostgreSQL.
- The runner requires the exact v0.24.2 predecessor image, a dedicated schema-owner credential, a distinct seed Secret, a stable shard identity, and a bounded receipt destination.

## Database migrations

- The one-shot runner executes a transactionally bounded TypeORM schema plan only when its canonical SQL digest matches the signed exact-v0.24.2 manifest, then uses the exact predecessor TypeORM MigrationExecutor to fake-record the 132 migrations already represented by that schema in the same transaction; it never calls TypeORM synchronize or writes ledger rows directly.
- It accepts only an object-free pristine schema or the exact bootstrap-produced 0130 state, under one PostgreSQL advisory lock. Restricted owner/runtime role safety is checked before mutation; partial ledgers, an empty ledger with objects, policy/object/owner/ACL drift, seed/catalogue/config drift, ordinary business data, and release-effect cohort objects fail closed.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: no.

## Security

- Before any database connection or schema mutation, the runner requires an explicit valid ADMIN_EMAIL; the bounded receipt excludes database URLs, passwords, password hashes, OAuth material, and all Secret payloads, and the stored administrator bcrypt hash is verified against ADMIN_PASSWORD without exposing either value.
- The signed contract pins the exact predecessor revision, release tag, backend digest, migration inventory, legacy RLS profile, advisory-lock namespace, seed profile, and receipt schema.
- The existing 0130-to-0131 bridge remains unchanged and continues to reject fresh, empty, partial, and drifted databases.
- Public authentication routing uses one shared exact-path policy for session bootstrap and unauthorized-response handling so newly supported public paths cannot silently drift between those controls.
- Only root signup and established invitation enrollment suppress the initial session probe; login remains session-aware and protected routes retain fail-closed validation, refresh, and redirection.

## Known limitations

- This artifact supports only fresh pooled PostgreSQL managed shards and does not provide portability evidence for the other supported database adapters.
- Cloud provisioning remains responsible for signature verification, immutable image selection, shard fencing, receipt retention, and enabling the default-off hook.

## Rollback

- Delete and recreate a failed brand-new shard from the provider-owned pristine boundary; do not repair its ledger or reuse a partially bootstrapped database.
- No existing installation is modified when the bootstrap remains disabled.
- Redeploy the previous frontend image or frontend host package; no API, configuration, or database rollback is required.

## Validation evidence

- Focused contract tests cover default-off behavior, immutable predecessor binding, pristine/exact-0130 classification, every fail-closed drift class, bounded receipt redaction, and Helm ordering.
- A PostgreSQL 16 qualification creates an object-free database, applies the exact predecessor migrations without synchronize, verifies every created seed/catalogue/config set plus empty ordinary tables and exact role/RLS/ACL ownership, proves idempotent exact-0130 recognition, and rejects deliberate ledger, object, role, policy, owner, ACL, password, audit-coverage, and data drift; missing or malformed administrator email fails before creating the target schema.
- Focused frontend tests cover root signup, established invitation enrollment, session-aware login and recovery pages, protected-route session validation, expired-session refresh, and exact path-boundary matching.
- Browser coverage verifies that anonymous signup renders without authentication or refresh probes and that a valid cookie session on login is restored and redirected without browser diagnostics.
